rules.explanation: A new <all_urls> or *://*/* host pattern lets the extension read and change every page you visit.
rules.title: Gains access to every website

rules.explanation: A periodic timer and a network call to a new domain in the same file: the extension keeps asking a server what to do.
rules.title: Polls a server on a timer

rules.explanation: New host patterns were added to host_permissions or content script matches.
rules.title: Gains access to more websites

rules.explanation: Content scripts now match more URLs, run in all frames, run before the page loads, or reach about:/data:/blob: frames.
rules.title: Injects code into more pages or frames

rules.explanation: A content script with world MAIN shares the page's JavaScript environment: it can read page variables, hook APIs and bypass the isolated world.
rules.title: Runs in the page's own JavaScript world

rules.explanation: chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts or userScripts.register can inject into pages the manifest never mentions.
rules.title: Registers content scripts at runtime

rules.explanation: APIs such as cookies, history, webRequest, tabs, scripting, debugger or nativeMessaging expose browsing data or code execution.
rules.title: Requests a sensitive browser API

rules.explanation: A new API permission that is not in the sensitive set.
rules.title: Requests a new browser API

rules.explanation: eval, new Function or a timer with a string body can run code that is not in the shipped files.
rules.title: Executes dynamically built code

rules.explanation: Setting an on* attribute to a string runs that string as JavaScript. Used by QuickLens to run server-supplied code on every page.
rules.title: Executes code through an event-handler attribute

rules.explanation: importScripts with a remote URL pulls executable code from outside the package.
rules.title: Loads scripts from a remote server

rules.explanation: importScripts is called with a non-literal argument.
rules.title: Loads scripts from a computed location

rules.explanation: A <script src="https://..."> in an extension page executes code from a server.
rules.title: Extension page loads a remote script

rules.explanation: javascript: URLs execute their content.
rules.title: Navigates to a javascript: URL

rules.explanation: The same file reads chrome.storage and executes strings, the pattern of a payload cached from a remote server.
rules.title: Runs code that was fetched into storage

rules.explanation: A network endpoint that earlier versions did not contact.
rules.title: Talks to a new domain

rules.explanation: The domain is common infrastructure (Google, GitHub, a public CDN, or the extension's own homepage).
rules.title: Talks to a new well-known domain

rules.explanation: The host of a request is computed, so it cannot be read from the code.
rules.title: Builds request URLs at runtime

rules.explanation: A declarativeNetRequest rule or webRequest listener removes or rewrites Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or similar headers, disabling the protections of every site.
rules.title: Removes security headers from web pages

rules.explanation: A declarativeNetRequest rule sets or appends Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or similar headers; a strict value is fine, a weakened one is not.
rules.title: Rewrites security headers on web pages

rules.explanation: A declarativeNetRequest redirect rule sends matching requests somewhere else; redirecting a login or update URL is a classic hijack.
rules.title: Redirects requests

rules.explanation: allowAllRequests rules switch off every blocking rule for matching frames.
rules.title: Exempts whole pages from blocking rules

rules.explanation: Dynamic declarativeNetRequest rules or webRequest header listeners can rewrite traffic in ways not visible in the package.
rules.title: Changes network rules at runtime

rules.explanation: chrome.scripting.executeScript or tabs.executeScript runs code in web pages on demand.
rules.title: Injects scripts into tabs programmatically

rules.explanation: Native messaging bridges the extension to a program on the computer.
rules.title: Talks to a native program

rules.explanation: document.createElement('script') is how remote code is injected into pages.
rules.title: Creates script elements

rules.explanation: Sources set from variables can point anywhere.
rules.title: Assigns computed URLs to src attributes

rules.explanation: Injected frames can load third-party pages inside sites.
rules.title: Creates iframes

rules.explanation: innerHTML with computed content can inject markup and scripts.
rules.title: Writes HTML from variables

rules.explanation: keydown, keypress, input or paste listeners in a content script can capture what you type.
rules.title: Content script listens to keystrokes or form input

rules.explanation: New submit, change, copy or unload listeners in a content script.
rules.title: Content script listens to page events

rules.explanation: Language, time zone, user agent or screen size are read; combined with a new server this is targeting logic.
rules.title: Collects device fingerprint details

rules.explanation: externally_connectable now lets pages send messages to the extension, turning it into a bridge for those sites.
rules.title: Websites can message the extension

rules.explanation: unsafe-eval, wasm-unsafe-eval or remote sources were added to the extension CSP.
rules.title: Weakens its own content security policy

rules.explanation: The update URL moved away from the store, so future versions come from elsewhere.
rules.title: Updates from a different server

rules.explanation: The listing is offered by a different developer than before. Extensions that turn malicious are usually sold first.
rules.title: Web Store publisher changed

rules.explanation: The listing disappeared, often because Google took it down for policy violations, while the installed copy keeps running.
rules.title: Removed from the Web Store

rules.explanation: A different key means a different publisher signed this version.
rules.title: Signing key changed

rules.explanation: The key in manifest.json does not derive to the extension ID; the files were tampered with or sideloaded.
rules.title: Files were not signed for this ID

rules.explanation: Long encoded strings, hex escapes, atob/fromCharCode or _0x identifiers appeared.
rules.title: Code became obfuscated

rules.explanation: Right-to-left overrides, isolates, zero-width characters or stray byte-order marks can make code read differently from how it runs (Trojan Source).
rules.title: Source contains invisible or bidirectional characters

rules.explanation: New .wasm modules are opaque to code review; their imports and behavior are not analyzed.
rules.title: Ships WebAssembly

rules.explanation: WebAssembly.instantiate or compile is called.
rules.title: Loads WebAssembly at runtime

rules.explanation: Some files were too large, too deeply nested or could not be read. Absence of findings there means nothing.
rules.title: Analysis was incomplete

rules.explanation: New static declarativeNetRequest rules.
rules.title: Adds network rules

rules.explanation: web_accessible_resources changed; pages can load these files.
rules.title: Exposes resources to websites

rules.explanation: Total code size grew or shrank by more than half.
rules.title: Package size changed a lot

rules.explanation: New or deleted files in the package.
rules.title: Files added or removed

rules.explanation: The extension presents itself under a different name.
rules.title: Name changed

rules.explanation: Routine version bump.
rules.title: Version changed

rules.explanation: Description, icons, background or other fields changed.
rules.title: Manifest fields changed
